mandatory_display.text: Do not exceed 110 km/h when riding solo, carrying a pillion or payload on an accessory-equipped motorcycle.

Do not load weight or install accessories incorrectly; doing so may affect the motorcycle's stability, handling characteristics and safe operation and could result in an accident causing serious injury or loss of life.

Royal Enfield cautions you against use of non-standard parts such as aftermarket and custom-made extended front forks, which may adversely affect performance and handling. Removing or altering original parts may adversely affect the performance of the motorcycle, causing an accident, which could result in serious injury or loss of life.

Do not ignore model/design specifications; doing so constitutes motorcycle and accessories misuse, which may adversely affect handling and performance, causing an accident which could result in serious injury or loss of life.

mandatory_display.text: Do not run the motorcycle if the malfunction indication remains ON continuously, as it can cause severe damage to the ECU and sensors; visit the nearest authorised Royal Enfield dealer to diagnose and rectify the EMS defect.

The ABS indicator is ON during the initial check-up (until or after the vehicle has run a particular distance/speed) and turns OFF if the system is OK; it lights up again in case of any ABS system malfunction. Do not run the motorcycle if the ABS indicator lamp remains continuously ON.
Always disconnect the black negative (-ve) battery cable first and then the red positive (+ve) cable when removing the battery connections.
Caution: when connecting the battery, connect the red positive (+ve) terminal first and then the black negative (-ve) terminal.
Caution: keep both battery terminal cables firmly connected to their terminals; failure to do so may damage the motorcycle electrical system.
Note: poor contact or loose fitment of the battery terminals may cause ECU failure.
In the rear-suspension setting table, tyre pressure is printed as one merged cell reading 32 psi that spans Front and Rear for both the rider-only and the laden rows.

source_object.exact_text:  Large surfaces such as fairings, windshields, backrests and luggage racks can adversely affect handling of the motorcycle. Use only Royal Enfield genuine motorcycle accessories which are model specific and follow installation procedure.
Therefore, the rider must be responsible for safe operation of the motorcycle when installing accessories or carrying additional weight.

 Re-check the luggage periodically to ensure it is secured and will not shift while riding. Accessories mounted loosely may affect the riding of the motorcycle and affect the handling and stability of the motorcycle.
 Do not exceed 110 km/h when riding solo, carrying a pillion or payload on an accessory equipped motorcycle.
Royal Enfield offers a range of Genuine Motorcycle Accessories that have been fully approved and extensively tested alongside the motorcycle.
 Do not load bulky items behind the rider or add weight to the handlebars or front forks.
 Keep luggage weight concentrated close to the motorcycle and as low as possible; this minimizes sudden shift in the motorcycle's center of gravity.
 Distribute weight evenly on both sides of the motorcycle.
Please adhere to the following guidelines when carrying a pillion, luggage or when fitting any accessories.

source_object.exact_text:  Do not run motorcycle in case the malfunction remains "ON" continuously as it can cause severe damage to the ECU & Sensors. Please visit the nearest authorised Royal Enfield dealer to diagnose & rectify the defect in the EMS.
 Do not run motorcycle in case the ABS indicator lamp continuously "ON".

Usage of frequency for motorcycle is very important for battery to be in good performance condition. If the motorcycle is being used very rarely or sparingly and the terminals are not disconnected the battery is bound to lose its charge and result in a dead battery.
For checking the battery voltage contact Royal Enfield Authorised Service Centre or battery service centre.
Always disconnect the black negative (-ve) battery cable first and then the red positive (+ve) cable while removing the battery connections.
The poor contact or loose fitment of battery terminals may cause ECU failure.

Keep the red (+ve) positive terminal and (-ve) negative terminal cables firmly connected to the respective battery terminals. Failure to do so may result in damage to the motorcycle electrical system.
Connect the red (+ve) positive terminal first and then connect black (-ve) negative terminal only.
Clean the wire terminals free from corrosion and keep the terminals coated with petroleum jelly.

source_object.exact_text: In-case your motorcycle is not going to be used for a month or more, the following precautions should be taken.
 Clean drive chain thoroughly and apply Royal Enfield recommended chain lubricant.
 Cover the silencer with suitable bags to prevent moisture entry. Set the motorcycle on its center stand.
 Remove charging circuit fuse from the fuse box.
 Store the battery in a cool, dry and well ventilated place.
 Drain the fuel completely from the fuel tank and induction system.

context.review_note: The manual's fuel-handling warnings (page 8: no smoking, open flames or sparks when refuelling or servicing the fuel system; page 27: gasoline vapour is highly explosive, fill only in a well-ventilated area) apply to draining fuel but are not linked here, because their existing dependency closure would add unrelated warnings.

source_object.exact_text:  If the motorcycle is not used for a month or longer, It is advised to disconnect battery terminals and remove the battery. Before refitting the battery in the motorcycle, check the battery voltage is within specification, if not, recharge it from authorized service workshop/ battery dealer.
 Wipe off excess lubricant after 5 minutes of application.
 Apply anti rust solutions on all plated parts. Take care not to apply this solution on chrome, rubber or painted parts. Store motorcycle in a clean covered area free of moisture and dust.
 Get the motorcycle serviced through a Royal Enfield Authorised Service Centre.
 For re-use after storage, it is preferable to get the motorcycle prepared through a Royal Enfield Authorised Service Centre to ensure the motorcycle is restored to its peak operating conditions.
* Do not mix DOT 4 or other brake fluid together.
